story.head: Special teams lean toward the Devils
paras: The Devils won the teams’ first meeting this season, 3-2 in New Jersey on Monday. The Devils come in at 16-8-0, the Blue Jackets at 9-13-0. This is a Metropolitan Division matchup, with the Devils second (tied for sixth in the NHL) and the Jackets seventh (tied for 28th).

The Devils have played better than their record (.667) says: their chances are worth about .728, and their goaltending has held them back. So have the Blue Jackets (.409 on chances worth .495), where their finishing has held them back.

The Devils draw more penalties than they take (2nd), rarely throw hits (3rd lowest) and keep things calm after the whistle (3rd lowest). New Jersey has scored 3.75 goals a game, the fourth most in the league. On the other side, the Blue Jackets lean on their stars as much as almost anyone (2nd most) and forecheck as hard as almost anyone (3rd). Columbus has scored 2.45 goals a game, the second fewest in the league. The Devils’ power play (6th) could do real damage against the Blue Jackets’ penalty kill (22nd). On top of that, the Blue Jackets’ defensemen shoot a lot, and the Devils’ not so much.

Jack Hughes (10 G / 20 A / 30 P in 24 GP) leads the Devils in scoring, with a point in six straight games against Columbus. Jesper Bratt (4 G / 18 A / 22 P in 24 GP) is next in line. For the Blue Jackets, Kent Johnson (9 G / 13 A / 22 P in 22 GP) leads the way in scoring. Zach Werenski (5 G / 16 A / 21 P in 22 GP) is next in line, with seven points in his last five games.
Connor Hellebuyck (8-1-0 / .898 SV% in 10 GS) is expected to start for New Jersey, and Cam Talbot (7-5-0 / .905 SV% in 12 GS) for Columbus.
